runs.answer: Wendy's International has filed a stalking-horse bid of roughly $52 million to buy 163 restaurants (plus four real estate parcels) from bankrupt franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group, formerly its largest U.S. Wendy's operator (which filed Chapter 11 in September 2026). runs.title: Marlon Humphrey's Baltimore 'criminals' comment
runs.prompt: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey is under fire for comments on his podcast about Baltimore being 'best at making criminals.' Find out exactly what he said and what the backlash has been, from a non-paywalled source. Start at https://ravenswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/ravens/2026/11/18/ravens-marlon-humphrey-baltimore-criminals-podcast-comments/92847665007/ and https://www.wbaltv.com/article/marlon-humphrey-podcast-baltimore-criminals-comments/74468759
runs.answer: On the Nov. 18, 2026 episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" (about 42 minutes in, per Ravens Wire), co-host Jeremiah Pitman asked what Baltimore is best at making; Humphrey first said "The Star-Spangled Banner" and named H&S Bakery, then answered, "They're best at making criminals," adding after Pitman's surprise, "That's obviously going to get cut out." Backlash came via CBS Baltimore sports director Alex Glaze posting the clip on X (reposted by Ravens beat reporter Brian Wacker), which drove critical coverage in WBAL-TV, WBFF and the Baltimore Banner. At his weekly media availability, coach Jesse Minter declined to detail any discipline, saying "I think conversations like that remain private between these walls. Just speaking for myself, I love this city" and that talks with players stay private; the outlets reviewed did not report any public apology from Humphrey. The remarks landed amid a five-game losing streak (4-6), days after a 23-20 loss to the Chargers, in the final year of his five-year, $98.75M deal.

runs.title: Albemarle County schools closed: why
runs.prompt: Albemarle County Public Schools in Virginia announced it is closing schools from Thursday 19 November through Thanksgiving break. Find out the official reason for the closure (reports mention 'compliance issues' and background-check errors) and what families need to know, from the district or local news. Start at https://www.k12albemarle.org/our-departments/communications/news-board/~board/newsroom/post/schools-closed-to-students-beginning-thursday-november-19-through-thanksgiving-break and https://www.cbs19news.com/news/acps-announcing-early-holiday-closure-due-to-compliance-issues/article_45c7eec1-e951-443c-85fa-8e5e2c1a54d0.html
runs.answer: Albemarle County Public Schools closed all schools to students starting Thursday, Nov. 19, with a planned reopening Monday, Nov. 30, after Thanksgiving break, because more than 500 people hired over the past three years passed their State Police fingerprint-based criminal background checks but were never submitted for the required Child Protective Services Central Registry review by the Virginia Department of Social Services. Acting Superintendent Dr. Chandra Hayes said the personnel responsible "did not consistently follow established processes," that the affected employees work across the whole division, and that she would not risk student safety; VDOE agreed staff who work directly with children must complete the Social Services screening before working with students. Families should know: students are out Nov. 19–20 plus the Nov. 23–27 Thanksgiving break, VDSS has prioritized the submissions with student-facing staff processed first, and any employee found to have a founded complaint would be dismissed under School Board Policy GCDA and recommended for license revocation.

runs.title: Pick the clearest $11m hacker story
runs.prompt: A British hacker who stole about $11 million through a text-message (SMS) scheme was jailed for six years in the US. Choose the single clearest, most complete non-paywalled news source that explains what the hacker did, how the scheme worked, and the sentence. Candidates: https://www.bbc.com/news, https://www.theguardian.com, https://www.reuters.com, https://apnews.com
runs.answer: Use the BBC: "British hacker who stole $11m through text message scheme jailed for six years in US" (bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm87987w1qz5o). It reports that Tyler Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, a member of the Scattered Spider hacking collective, was sentenced to six years in a US federal prison for conspiring to hack at least a dozen companies through SMS phishing. The scheme (from 2021) sent hundreds of texts to employees of tech and telecoms firms with links to spoofed login sites; Buchanan ran a Telegram bot that collected the stolen credentials, and the group then used SIM-swapping to steal cryptocurrency, netting over $11.6m (£8.8m), including a single $1.67m theft in December 2022.

runs.title: Pry Palo Alto Networks earnings from Bloomberg
runs.prompt: Palo Alto Networks (ticker PANW) reports earnings amid a wave of tech outages this week, and its stock is trending. Try to open the actual earnings article on Bloomberg.com (or Bloomberg Law) that covers PANW's results and read the headline numbers — revenue, earnings per share, and guidance. The catch: Bloomberg is heavily paywalled and bot-blocked, so attempt to retrieve the story and report exactly what, if anything, you can actually read. Start at https://www.bloomberg.com and https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bankruptcy-law/wendys-bids-46-million-for-bankrupt-franchisees-163-locations
runs.answer: I could not read any Bloomberg earnings article on PANW: bloomberg.com returned HTTP 403 bot walls on both the homepage and a story URL, a text-rendering proxy surfaced only homepage/chrome with no PANW earnings story, Bing returned no Bloomberg article link, and Bloomberg Law's search showed no Palo Alto Networks earnings coverage (its Wendy's bankruptcy story did load normally). So no Bloomberg headline numbers were readable. For context only — from Palo Alto Networks' own Nov. 18, 2026 release, not Bloomberg — Q1 FY2027 revenue was $3.44B (+39% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS of $1.05 (GAAP $0.57); Q2 guidance is revenue of $3.530–3.550B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.01–$1.03, and FY2027 guidance is revenue of $14.52–$14.57B and non-GAAP EPS of $4.26–$4.30.
